title: Job 38
paragraphs: ¹ Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: ² "Who is this who darkens counsel with words devoid of knowledge? ³ Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me. ⁴ Where were you when I laid the earth's foundations? Tell me, if you know so much. ⁵ Who determined its dimensions? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?

⁶ On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone — ⁷ while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy? ⁸ Who shut the sea behind its doors when it burst from the womb, ⁹ when I made the clouds its garment and wrapped it in thick darkness, ¹⁰ when I fixed its limits and set its doors and bars in place?

¹¹ And said, 'This far you may come and no farther; here is where your proud waves halt'? ¹² Have you ever commanded the morning, or shown the dawn its place, ¹³ so that it could take hold of the earth's edges and shake the wicked out of it? ¹⁴ The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its features stand out like folds of a garment. ¹⁵ Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.

¹⁶ Have you walked in the recesses of the deep, or explored the springs of the sea? ¹⁷ Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness? ¹⁸ Have you comprehended the vast expanse of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this. ¹⁹ What is the way to the dwelling of light? And where does darkness reside? ²⁰ Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their homes?

²¹ Surely you know — you were already born! How many years have you lived? ²² Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the armories of hail, ²³ which I reserve for times of trouble, for days of war and battle? ²⁴ What is the way to the place where lightning is dispersed, or the place where the east wind is scattered over the earth?

²⁶ to send rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness where there is no human being, ²⁷ to satisfy a desolate wasteland and make it burst into green life? ²⁸ Does the rain have a father? Who fathers the drops of dew? ²⁹ From whose womb comes the ice? Who gives birth to the frost from the heavens ³⁰ when the waters grow hard as stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen?

³¹ Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion's belt? ³² Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons, or lead out the Bear with its cubs? ³³ Do you know the laws of heaven? Can you impose them on the earth? ³⁴ Can you raise your voice to the clouds and make a flood of water cover you? ³⁵ Can you send lightning bolts on their way? Will they report back to you, 'Here we are'?

³⁶ Who gave wisdom to the heart, or understanding to the mind? ³⁷ Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the heavens ³⁸ when the dust becomes hard as iron and the clods of earth stick together? ³⁹ Can you hunt prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the lions ⁴⁰ when they crouch in their dens, or lie in wait in their lairs?
⁴¹ Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God, wandering about for lack of food?
